claims.statement: Gateway TLS is independent of internal TLS: with_tls builds an acceptor requiring client certificates when a CA is supplied, while mTLS startup uses a verified certificate CN and refuses missing CN rather than trusting a startup cn parameter.

The control TCP protocol uses TLS and extracted NodeIdentity only when an acceptor is configured; otherwise it handles plaintext with no peer identity, and verified registration requires Worker role and a matching worker ID or address.
Shuffle service startup conditionally enables internal TLS and client CA authentication, but does not extract NodeIdentity or bind a worker request identity to its certificate in that service.

ManagementService starts a plaintext tonic server without TLS or an authentication interceptor; its administrative handlers do not resolve principals or check AclStore, and DrainWorker can schedule work after version, argument, admission, and operation-store checks.

The CLI management client defaults unqualified addresses to HTTP and connects without configuring identity credentials; runtime DataPlaneClient strips HTTP/HTTPS prefixes and uses a raw TCP connection.
The Raft peer listener accepts raw TcpStreams and passes them directly to peer connection handling rather than the control worker TLS acceptor.

NodeIdentity supports canonical role/node identity encodings and compatibility forms, including fallback of otherwise unrecognized bare CNs to the CLI role; parsing alone is not administrative authorization.

Control TLS requires certificate/key paths and a CA when client authentication is required; TlsCertificateReloader rebuilds and swaps acceptors with additional CA roots for overlap rather than replacing existing negotiated streams.

Gateway authentication modes map off to privileged System, JWT subjects to Jwt principals, verified certificate CNs to CertCn, and password-authenticated users to ScramUser; System bypasses gateway ACL checks.
RoleCatalog is an in-memory password-authentication catalog storing salted SCRAM material and optional MD5 hashes, separate from ACL grants; password updates replace both representations.
JwtVerifier supports HS256 using supplied/cached keys, requires sub, checks exp only if present, and does not validate issuer or audience or fetch discovery keys in its verify path.

CLI OIDC gateway startup supplies a built-in default signing key, and gateway startup has a verifier-absent fallback using the token as JWT identity, so the OIDC label alone is not production identity-provider integration.
AuthMode parsing maps unknown strings to Off, whereas CLI run_start normalizes and validates an allowlist and returns RS-0002 for unknown authentication modes.
Constructing a gateway in mTLS authentication mode does not itself install a TLS acceptor; TLS is installed through the separate with_tls builder.
The current AclStore grant, revoke, and lookup operations act on an in-memory map, prefer object grants over namespace grants, compare minimum roles, and bypass checks for the identity string system.

Gateway mutation authorization treats missing sessions as System and connectionless dispatch as trusted; read access likewise uses a System default without a connection, so these paths must not substitute for authenticated sessions.

Gateway relation access requires Viewer in the session namespace and additionally requires session-namespace Admin for non-System cross-namespace catalog-view reads; denials return SQLSTATE 42501 with RS-2401 or RS-2402.

Gateway mutations consult shared pgwire_mutation_policy before execution, using session identity, namespace, and resource; insufficient roles produce 42501/RS-2401 and attempt an audit event, with PipelineOwner for ordinary creation and Admin for secret DDL and administrative changes.

SUBSCRIBE reuses the SELECT ACL/namespace gate before retention lookup, snapshot reads, or stream admission; focused tests prove denied snapshot/replay and cross-namespace requests do not call readers or consume stream slots, while a Viewer grant allows admission.

CLI mutation authorization uses local ClientIdentity roles and shared CLI_MUTATION_POLICY, but ClientIdentity is caller-constructed metadata defaulting to Admin rather than proof of verified bearer or certificate credentials; local denials are not server-side management authorization.

SecretStore owns encrypted catalog entries and the active KEK provider; envelope encryption uses local DEKs, AES-256-GCM payload encryption, and provider-wrapped DEKs, while SHOW SECRETS returns metadata rather than plaintext.

Default gateway/control secret stores use EnvKekProvider::from_env_or_default, deriving a key from RS_SECRET_KEK or a deterministic fallback when absent; KMS selection requires explicit provider/store injection rather than merely an ARN.

AwsKmsKekProvider uses signed KMS Encrypt/Decrypt to wrap locally generated DEKs with no local-encryption fallback; local protocol fixtures do not qualify AWS IAM enforcement and the real AWS permission test is explicitly ignored.
Gateway secret DDL currently targets namespace ID 0 and uses pgwire as the store audit actor rather than the authenticated principal actor.
Live control secret-token issuance requires a verified Worker certificate and issues a 300-second namespace-0 token bound to its node ID without a per-secret assignment or ACL check in that branch.

WorkerSecretManager verifies token identity, expiry, nonce and AES-GCM authentication before retaining plaintext in a bounded memory-only cache, removes expired entries on reads, and uses a token key derived from the public worker identity string rather than a private key.
ALTER SECRET increments its version and emits a rotation notification; the runtime responds to SecretRotated by requesting a fresh token and resolves issued tokens into its in-memory secret manager.

KEK rotation locks out competing store operations, stages all rewrapped envelopes before atomic publication, leaves stored envelopes unchanged on staging failure, and uses a cancellation-resistant spawned commit that waits for durability before dropping the old provider.

Interrupted KEK rotation recovery requires retaining both keys, reopening with RetainedKekProvider and retrying rotation; the retained provider writes with its first provider and tries both on reads, and a shared store per catalog is required because independent instances are not coordinated by its lock.

FileAuditLog appends JSONL under a process-local lock, opens the file during append, propagates I/O errors and does not fsync; gateway denial, secret store, control TLS, and CLI audit callers discard failures, so audit is not fail-closed or transactional with mutations.

Secret audit/listing tests verify plaintext literals are absent from audit and metadata, with rotation tests also inspecting encrypted catalog artifacts; diagnostic redaction masks recognized assignments, bearer values, URL credentials and key-like input, but FileAuditLog itself does not sanitize arbitrary event fields.

Repository security documents differ in scope: the readiness report records a closed internal assessment while the threat model says a commissioned independent report is not yet available; their broad boundary statements do not establish identical protection on all current listeners.
